items.stem: How does SDM treat permanent FTE staff versus Contractors?

options.text: FTE staff are augmented from the HR system of record; Contractors are fully maintained in SDM (account, email, initial job)
Both are created from scratch in SDM
Both are loaded from the HR system of record and only augmented
FTE staff are fully maintained in SDM; Contractors come from the HR feed

items.explanation: Permanent staff come from a system of record into DDH and SDM augments them; Contractors have no HR feed, so SDM fully maintains them — provisioning the security account and email and creating an initial job linked to the manager.

misconceptions.b: FTE staff already exist in the system of record — SDM augments rather than creates them.
misconceptions.c: Contractors are not in the HR system of record; SDM maintains them end to end.
misconceptions.d: It's the reverse: FTE = augment, Contractor = full maintenance.

items.stem: Which supplemental attributes does SDM augment onto staff records?

options.text: Service Area, Support Languages, and Proxy Addresses
Salary, tax code, and bank account
Attendance Areas, District Programs, and Municipal Divisions
SMTP host, sender address, and job codes

items.explanation: SDM augments staff with Service Area, Support Languages, and Proxy Addresses — the supplemental data the source doesn't provide.

misconceptions.b: Payroll fields belong to the HR system of record, not SDM's augmentation layer.
misconceptions.c: Those are links made on the Schools page (S3.1), not staff augmentation fields.
misconceptions.d: Those are email-notification settings (S2.4), not staff attributes.

items.stem: What is true about the access rights FTEs and Contractors receive?

options.text: Both get the same access rights relative to their assigned manager
Contractors always get fewer rights than FTEs
Access depends on whether the person is paid or a volunteer
Only FTEs receive access; Contractors get none

items.explanation: Access is keyed to the assigned manager, not the staff type — FTEs and Contractors get the same access rights relative to their manager.

misconceptions.b: Staff type doesn't reduce access; the manager determines it.
misconceptions.c: Paid-vs-volunteer affects nothing about access; the manager does.
misconceptions.d: Contractors do receive access — the same as FTEs, relative to their manager.

items.stem: A volunteer classroom tutor is starting and has no record anywhere yet. What does SDM do for them on the Staff page?

options.text: Fully maintains them — provisions a security account and email and creates an initial job linked to their manager
Waits for the HR system of record to load them, then augments the record
Refuses them because volunteers aren't staff
Creates the school they will work at

items.explanation: A volunteer is a Contractor — part of the HR-gap staffing SDM owns. With no HR feed, SDM fully maintains them: security account, email, and an initial job linked to the assigned manager.

misconceptions.b: There is no HR feed for contractors/volunteers; SDM maintains them directly.
misconceptions.c: Contractors explicitly include volunteers and student teachers.
misconceptions.d: Schools come from HRAD (S3.1); creating one is not part of staffing a contractor.

items.stem: A new permanent FTE is being loaded and their name conflicts with an existing record. How is this handled in SDM?

options.text: Resolve it on the Staff page using the On-Hold feature
Delete the existing staff record so the new one can load
Convert the new FTE to a Contractor to dodge the conflict
Create a brand-new school to hold the duplicate name

items.explanation: New FTEs coming onboard with a name conflict are resolved with the On-Hold feature; on-hold/merge events can also fire notifications (S2.4).

misconceptions.b: Deleting a real record to clear a name clash is destructive and not the workflow.
misconceptions.c: Conversion changes the staff type; it isn't a tool for resolving name conflicts.
misconceptions.d: Schools are unrelated to a staff name conflict.

items.stem: A contractor who has worked for months is hired as permanent staff. What is the appropriate action in SDM?

options.text: Use FTE↔Contractor conversion to convert the existing record
Delete the contractor and wait for the HR system of record, since FTEs can't be edited in SDM
Nothing — staff type can never change in SDM
Move the record to the Vendor Reps page

items.explanation: SDM supports conversion both ways (FTE↔Contractor), so you convert the existing record rather than re-keying it.

misconceptions.b: There's no need to delete and wait — conversion is supported in SDM.
misconceptions.c: Conversion in both directions is explicitly supported.
misconceptions.d: Vendor Reps are 3rd-party vendor representatives, distinct from contractors and FTEs (S1.4).

items.stem: In one or two sentences, explain the difference between how SDM handles an FTE versus a Contractor, and name one thing SDM does for a Contractor that it does not do for an FTE.
rubric: States FTEs come from the HR system of record and SDM augments them (e.g. Service Area / Support Languages / Proxy Addresses)
States Contractors are fully maintained in SDM because there is no HR feed
Names a full-maintenance action SDM does for a Contractor: provision the security account/email, or create an initial job linked to the manager
items.sampleAnswer: An FTE already exists in the HR system of record, so SDM only augments the record (Service Area, Support Languages, Proxy Addresses). A Contractor has no HR feed, so SDM fully maintains them — for example provisioning their security account and email and creating an initial job linked to their manager.
